note: Every voice this benchmark can run, as data rather than code. A model is added by appending a row here - no new adapter unless it needs a runtime nobody has wired yet. `sizeGb` is the ACTUAL download for the named variant, not the repository total: a repository carrying fp32, fp16 and int4 of the same weights reports three times what a run costs.

voicePreference.why: The corpus is international news read for a British-English listener. Kokoro's `b` prefix is British - bm_george, bm_lewis, bf_emma, bf_alice - and where a model has no labelled British voice the nearest neutral one is used and the row says so.
voicePreference.fallback: If a model publishes no accent labels, take the first voice and record `accentKnown: false` so a listening test is not told an accent it cannot verify.

kokoro-js.note: transformers.js cannot load these - `style_text_to_speech_2` is registered only as an encoder there and its text-to-speech pipeline throws Unsupported model type.

transformers.js.note: Exactly four architectures are registered for text-to-speech, and musicgen is the fourth. Supertonic hard-fails without a speaker embedding rather than choosing one.

onnxruntime-genai.note: NOT WIRED. These ship as several ONNX graphs (text_embed, talker, audio_encoder, code2wav) driven by a generation loop, so they need their own runner rather than a one-call adapter.

llama.cpp.loads: Orpheus (Llama-3.2-3B backbone) and NeuTTS Air (Qwen2.5-0.5B backbone)
llama.cpp.note: A GGUF voice is TWO models and only the first is in the file. llama.cpp runs the backbone, which emits audio codec tokens rather than audio; a separate neural codec decoder - SNAC for Orpheus, NeuCodec for NeuTTS - turns those integers into a waveform and does not run in llama.cpp at all. Prebuilt CPU wheels stop at 0.3.19 for cp312, so that is the pin: building from source on 4 vCPU costs more than the benchmark.

nemo-speech.cpp.note: PROOF THAT A GGUF IS NOT A LLAMA.CPP FILE. Magpie's GGUF will not load in llama.cpp: it is an encoder-decoder predicting 8 codebooks with frame stacking and a local transformer, and NVIDIA ships its own ggml-based runtime for it. The linux-x86_64 CPU archive is 4.4 MB and is downloaded rather than built. The CLI reloads its weights per invocation, so this arm's real-time factor includes model load per chunk.

models.name: Kokoro-82M
models.note: Kept as the control. Measured 2.32x SLOWER than fp32 on the runner for identical audio.

models.name: KittenTTS nano 0.8
models.blocked: kokoro-js cannot load it: the repository ships kitten_config.json and voices.npz but NO tokenizer.json, which kokoro-js fetches unconditionally. Verified 2026-09-13. Needs its own adapter over raw onnxruntime plus a phonemiser.

models.name: KittenTTS mini 0.8
models.blocked: kokoro-js cannot load it: the repository ships kitten_config.json and voices.npz but NO tokenizer.json, which kokoro-js fetches unconditionally. Verified 2026-09-13. Needs its own adapter over raw onnxruntime plus a phonemiser.

models.name: Supertonic TTS
models.note: The transformers.js default TTS model. Voices are F1-F5 and M1-M5 with no accent labels, so the accent must be judged by ear. Upstream GitHub is archived.

models.name: MMS-TTS English
models.note: A control rather than a candidate: it needs no speaker embedding, so if this arm fails the harness is the problem and not the model. Non-commercial, so it could never ship.

models.name: Chatterbox multilingual
models.note: Ships a complete ONNX Runtime recipe on its own model card - four graphs plus a sampling loop. Weights stream to the runner cache and are never committed. Watermarking is off for the measurement and would be on for anything published.

models.name: Qwen3-TTS 0.6B
models.blocked: Runtime not wired. Ships a cpu_int4 variant at 1.5 GB, which is the most plausible AR candidate on size alone: against the runner's measured ~23.7 GB/s that is roughly 16 backbone steps a second against a 12.5 Hz frame rate.

models.name: Higgs Audio v3 TTS
models.blocked: Runtime not wired, AND the licence is non-commercial. The repository totals 57 GB because it carries six variants; the cpu_int4 one is 3.59 GB.

models.name: Orpheus 3B 0.1 finetuned
models.note: The requested repository publishes 26 quantisations of the same weights, 929 MB to 6.3 GB; sizeGb is the Q4_K_M download (1.95 GB) plus the SNAC decoder, not the 57 GB catalogue. Voices are tara, leah, jess, leo, dan, mia, zac, zoe and none is labelled British, so the accent must be judged by ear. An AR model at 3B on 4 vCPU is the slowest thing this harness has been asked to run - that is the measurement.

models.name: NeuTTS Air

reference.name: dave
reference.why: NeuTTS is a cloning model with no built-in speaker: infer() requires reference codes and the reference transcript. The samples are in the GitHub repository, which is not gated, unlike the weights.

models.requiresToken: HF_TOKEN, for the codec ENCODER only. `neucodec` refuses every substitute by name rather than by content - its _from_pretrained opens with `assert model_id in ["neuphonic/neucodec", "neuphonic/distill-neucodec"]` - and both are gated, so no mirror can stand in. The backbone and the ONNX decoder need no token and are taken from ungated mirrors.
models.note: Two of the three artefacts are ungated substitutes and each is named, because the row is what a later reader will trust. The requested neuphonic/neutts-air-q4-gguf is Q4_0 at 502 MB; the backbone used is a community requant at Q4_K_M, 569 MB. The decoder is an ungated mirror of the int8 ONNX artifact. Getting here took five runs: the install deadlock needed torchao pinned to 0.13.0 - the window satisfying both neucodec's floor of >=0.12.0 and torchtune's import of torchao.dtypes.nf4tensor, removed in 0.14.0 - and the phonemiser needed an explicit language because a local .gguf path has no repository name to infer one from.

models.name: MagpieTTS Multilingual 357M
models.note: The one row that proves the vocabulary page right: this GGUF does NOT load in llama.cpp. It is an encoder-decoder predicting 8 codebooks with frame stacking, and NVIDIA ships NeMo-Speech.cpp for it. The runtime is a 4.4 MB released binary rather than a source build. Its CLI reloads weights per invocation, so this arm's real-time factor includes model load per chunk and is charitable to nothing.
